messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall — SLO breach detected for /streaming/generate (p99 latency). Alerting policy: streaming-p99 > 1800ms for 5m. Affected region: us-west-2. Potential impact: tail stalls and streaming stalls reported in traces.
alex: taking it — I'm oncall. kicking off triage.
maya: saw the alerts too, p95 jumped a bit earlier. dashboards show a big tail at ~23:14 UTC.
priya: linking traces — several streams show stall where server-side token emission pauses for 2-6s then resumes.
jason: also seeing spike in GPU error counters on node gpu-wn-42 (kv-serving pool). infra-bot posted nvidia metrics 60s ago.
alex: nate, can you pull node logs and gpu telemetry?
nate: on it. grabbing nvidia-smi & dmesg.
ate: paste: ```
$ nvidia-smi -q -i 2 | egrep 'Temperature|ECC|Clocks|Throttle'
GPU Current Temp : 95 C
ECC Errors (Corrected) : 124
ECC Errors (Uncorrected) : 3
Supports Active PwrMgt: Yes
Clocks Throttle Reason : Thermal
```
alex: ugh. ECC uncorrected > 0 and thermal 95C. that explains flakey stall behavior.
maya: dmesg shows repeated GPU reset messages and NVML recoveries. snippet: ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12346.001234] nvidia: GPU 2: Driver detached.
```
priya: customer-facing impact? any customer errors / 5xx?
jason: infra traces show retransmits but app returned 200 for most, just delayed streaming frames. a handful of p50->p99 escalations for customers on high-throughput routes.
emily: metrics: ~0.6% increase in user-observed streaming stalls; support tickets flagged one weird session with multiple partial responses.
alex: mitigation plan: 1) fail fast: cordon + drain gpu-wn-42, 2) migrate workloads to hot spare pool, 3) reduce concurrency/disable batching on streaming route to reduce load, 4) alert customers if degradation > 5% beyond 30m.
nate: starting drain: ```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-wn-42
kubectl drain gpu-wn-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
infra-bot: node gpu-wn-42 cordoned, pods evicted: 12. Replica set autoscaler started to recreate pods in pool-hot-spare-1.
priya: can we switch streaming traffic to fallback model variant (quantized small model) for affected tenants? that reduces per-token GPU pressure.
alex: yes — trigger gradual traffic cutover for non-SLA customers first. jason, can you prepare a canary?
jason: canary ready: redirecting 10% traffic to model-redwood-small-qtz in us-west-2. monitoring latency + quality.
maya: also lowering max concurrent requests per instance from 8 -> 4 for streaming route to lower queueing.
emily: real-time dashboards show p99 starting to drop as pods land in spare pool and concurrency lowered. improvement visible at +90s.
ops-bot: Incident note: CPU fallback invoked for 3 pods due to unavailable GPU device; latency for those requests increased but no stalls.
alex: good. keep node quarantined. we should run healthcheck on gpu-wn-42 before rejoin. priya, can you run NV diagnostic?
priya: running vendor diag, but logs show ECC uncorrected >0 which suggests potential hardware degradation. I'm opening a ticket with vendor and attaching logs.
nate: I attempted driver rebind but node produced repeated ECC increases on reboot. suspect flaky memory region.
jason: we saw downstream effect on KV cache usage: some streaming sessions hit cache miss -> larger seq lengths -> more GPU memory pressure -> exacerbated thermal. fixed by reducing max sequence length for in-flight sessions via runtime config.
maya: plan to implement runtime safeguard: if node ECC corrected spikes > threshold, automatically evacuate and route to fallback. file a follow-up task?
emily: customers impacted: 7 tenants experienced elevated p99s; 2 reported degraded UX. I drafted a message for Customer Success to send to affected accounts.
alex: send now to CS with suggested text. include ETA for follow-up and note we mitigated live — temporary fallback in place.
emily: sending. CS copy: "We observed transient streaming delays between 23:12–23:18 UTC in us-west-2. Root cause: GPU node hardware degradation causing intermittent stalls. Our mitigation: evicted traffic off the affected node and routed to healthy pool; small-model fallback enabled for non-SLA traffic. Engineers are investigating; we will provide a full post-incident report."
priya: vendor ticket created: TICKET-9987, severity high, logs attached. vendor asked for full coredump & nvml logs, collecting now.
ate: I've tagged node gpu-wn-42 with 'quarantine' and set autoscaler to avoid scheduling there.
jason: rolling a quick runtime patch to implement transient stall detection: if emission gap > 1.2s then serve from fallback pool and mark trace. small patch pushed to canary.
alex: good. let’s keep mitigation for 1 hour then reassess. once vendor confirms, we'll RMA if hardware confirmed.
maya: postmortem items: - create auto-evacuate runbook for ECC uncorrected > 1, - expose GPU thermal+ECC alert to oncall primary earlier (reduce threshold), - add node-level preemptive drain when corrected ECC growth rate > X/min.
ops-bot: created incident ticket INC-2026-345 and postmortem stub.
emily: support queue: no new high-severity tickets in last 20m. current user impact trending down.
alex: any objections to marking incident as mitigated and moving to monitoring?
priya: +1. vendor will continue analysis; we keep node offline.
jason: will follow up with quality checks on canary traffic for the next 2 hours.
maya: adding owner for runbook item: maya.
emily: I'll prepare the customer-facing postmortem draft after vendor confirmation.
alex: thanks team. incident mitigated -> moving to monitoring. will update status if vendor reports RMA or deeper fix needed. :thumbsup:
